equivalents.note: The Tibetan has only rnam gsum, 'the three (kinds)', for tini pāṭem̐ and no word of its own for pāṭa; the comment likewise has rnam gsum for pāṭatraya (cp.16.m2).

The Tibetan line has no word for ṭākali: it reads 'the sky became the unstruck sound' (nam mkha' gzhom med sgra ru gyur), putting Munidatta's gloss (anāhataśabda, cp.16.m4) in its place, while the comment only transliterates the word (Ta ge).
In the Rativajra verse the Tibetan has mkhas rnams, 'the wise', where the Sanskrit has buddhaiḥ, perhaps reading budha, 'wise', for buddha.
Here the Tibetan renders pramatta as rab tu dgyes pa, 'greatly delighted', not with myos pa, 'drunk', which it uses for the same word in the song and elsewhere in the comment.
For nirvāṇasarovara the Tibetan has mya ngan las 'das pa'i mtsho'i tshal, 'the lake-grove of nirvāṇa', as if reading -vana, 'grove', for -vara.
In the quoted verse de nyid rnam par mi rtog pa stands for tattvaṃ yan na vikalpyate, but de nyid can equally be read as 'that itself', so the Tibetan does not mark tattva as a term.

questions: bhaga (cp.16.m2): a false match. The Bengali ভগ comes from bhagnāḥ and bhagnaṃ, 'broken' (the Tibetan has 'joms and bcom), not from bhaga; the segment has no bhaga, so no equivalent is given.

mandala (cp.16.m2): in the Rativajra verse the Tibetan has gsang sngags sbyor ba mnyam med pa, 'the unequalled application of secret mantra', with no dkyil 'khor; mnyam med pa stands roughly where the Sanskrit has maṇḍalaṃ, so the translators' text may have read a different word there. Left unmatched (the verse line cp.16.1b already has dkyil 'khor).

gagana-ganga (cp.16.m6): the Tibetan has no word for Gaṅgā. Where the Sanskrit has gaganagaṅgā it reads nam mkhar 'khor ba, 'circling in the sky', which looks like an echo of its rendering of the song's gaaṇāṅgaṇa as nam mkha'i 'khor sa (cp.16.5a) rather than a rendering of gaganagaṅgā. Left unmatched.

mahasukha, matta, trailokya (cp.16.m5): the Tibetan comment is shorter than the Sanskrit here and omits mahāsukharasa, pramattaḥ and the clause on the three worlds (tribhuvanasya grahopekṣāṃ karoti), so it has no equivalents for them in this segment; all three are matched elsewhere in the song.

matta: myos pa is marked clear, since it plainly means 'drunk' and has no other sense, but the glossary also lists myos pa under mada ('ichor', song 9), where the Tibetan renders mada as intoxication. A whole-text search will count those occurrences as matta too; the reviewer may prefer to keep the form under one term only, or downgrade it.

nayaka (cp.16.4b): 'dren byed, 'one who leads', plainly renders nāyaka here (the comment has 'dren pa for nāyakatva, cp.16.m5), but it is marked likely because 'dren, 'lead, draw', is a common verb in the commentary and could be caught by a whole-text search in other senses.
